# dsterf

> Computes all eigenvalues of a real symmetric tridiagonal matrix using the.

<section class="usage">

## Usage

```js
import dsterf from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/base/dsterf';
```

### Layout API

Takes a storage layout (`order`) and leading dimensions, like CBLAS/LAPACKE.

```js
dsterf( N, d, strideD, e, strideE ) → integer
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Order of the matrix<br>Requires `N ≥ 0` |
| `d` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length N</sub> | **in/out** · Input array |
| ↳ `strideD` | `integer` | `d` stride length |
| `e` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length N - 1</sub> | **in/out** · Input array |
| ↳ `strideE` | `integer` | `e` stride length |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `N`: The order of the matrix. $N \ge 0$.
- `d`: On entry, the n diagonal elements of the tridiagonal matrix. On exit, if `INFO = 0`, the eigenvalues in ascending order.
- `e`: On entry, the (n-1) subdiagonal elements of the tridiagonal matrix. On exit, E has been destroyed.

</details>

**Returns** `integer`: info status code

**Throws**

- `RangeError` first argument must be a nonnegative integer

### Strided (ndarray) API

Takes explicit strides and offsets for every array. Use it for views, sub-matrices and non-unit strides.

```js
dsterf.ndarray( N, d, strideD, offsetD, e, strideE, offsetE ) → info: integer
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Order of the matrix<br>Requires `N ≥ 0` |
| `d` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length N</sub> | **in/out** · Diagonal elements (length N); on exit, eigenvalues in ascending order |
| ↳ `strideD` | `integer` | Stride length for `d` |
| ↳ `offsetD` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `d` |
| `e` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length N - 1</sub> | **in/out** · Off-diagonal elements (length N-1); destroyed on exit |
| ↳ `strideE` | `integer` | Stride length for `e` |
| ↳ `offsetE` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for `e` |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `N`: The order of the matrix. $N \ge 0$.
- `d`: On entry, the n diagonal elements of the tridiagonal matrix. On exit, if `INFO = 0`, the eigenvalues in ascending order.
- `e`: On entry, the (n-1) subdiagonal elements of the tridiagonal matrix. On exit, E has been destroyed.

</details>

**Returns** `info: integer`: 0 on success, >0 if failed to converge (number of unconverged elements)

**Throws**

- `RangeError` first argument must be a nonnegative integer

### Status codes

An `info` status code: `0` on success. A positive value reports a numerical condition such as a singular pivot or a failure to converge (see the description). Invalid arguments throw instead of returning a negative `info`. Returns immediately when `N <= 1`.

The reference documents `INFO` as:

-   `= 0`: successful exit
-   `< 0`: if `INFO = -i`, the i-th argument had an illegal value
-   `> 0`: the algorithm failed to find all of the eigenvalues in a total of $30 \, N$ iterations; if `INFO = i`, then i elements of E have not converged to zero.

</section>

<!-- /.usage -->

<section class="notes">

## Notes

-   `dsterf()` corresponds to the reference LAPACK routine [`DSTERF`](https://github.com/Reference-LAPACK/lapack/blob/v3.12.0/SRC/dsterf.f).

</section>

<!-- /.notes -->

<section class="examples">

## Examples

```js
import discreteUniform from '@stdlib/random/array/discrete-uniform/lib/index.js';
import dsterf from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/base/dsterf';

/** @type {{ dtype: 'float64' }} */
const opts = {
	'dtype': 'float64'
};
const N = 3;
const d = discreteUniform( N, -10, 10, opts );
const e = discreteUniform( N, -10, 10, opts );

// Using the standard interface:
let out = dsterf( N, d, 1, e, 1 );
console.log( out );

// Using the ndarray interface:
out = dsterf.ndarray( N, d, 1, 0, e, 1, 0 );
console.log( out );
```

</section>

<!-- /.examples -->

<section class="reference-notes">

## Reference notes

The mathematical description from the reference LAPACK 3.12.0 source of `DSTERF`. Indices are the 1-based Fortran indices of the source.

### Purpose

DSTERF computes all eigenvalues of a symmetric tridiagonal matrix using the Pal-Walker-Kahan variant of the QL or QR algorithm.

</section>
